newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish chief of staff to Cyprus over missile row.
newsitem.headline: Turkish chief of staff to Cyprus over missile row.

text.p: Turkish Chief of Staff Ismail Hakki Karadayi will travel to north Cyprus on Monday amid a row over the Cypriot government's planned deployment of Russian missiles on the divided island.

In a brief statement released on Saturday, the foreign ministry said Karadayi and a military delegation would visit the Turkish north of the island on Monday for a two-day visit on the invitation of Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.

Turkey has threatened military action against Cyprus to stop it deploying Russian anti-aircraft missiles and said it might occupy an abandoned tourist resort on the island if the Cypriot government did not back down.
Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has accused Greece of encouraging the Cypriot government to create a missile crisis in the Mediterranean.
NATO allies Ankara and Athens almost came to blows a year ago over a deserted islet in the Aegean Sea.
The West has expressed concern at the latest flare-up and Washington is to send an envoy to the island over the weekend to try to reduce the tension.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded northern Cyprus after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.

Turkey has some 30,000 troops in the northern third of Cyprus which declared itself a Turkish Cypriot state but is only recognised by Ankara. The internationally recognised Greek Cypriot government in the south commands a national guard of over 10,000 troops and is backed militarily by Athens.
